thread:
marco.sre: opening war room for an intermittent 5xx spike hitting hosted inference in ap-northeast-1. started ~09:14 UTC, still seeing ~2-5% errors on /v1/generate tiered by customer plan
anya.eng-runtime: seeing elevated 502s at the edge -> backend shows 504s from runtime pods. stack traces show 'kv cache stall' lines occasionally
devon.ops: pulled metrics: connection queue depth up, p95 latency for inference loop jumped from 120ms to 520ms around 09:13-09:18 UTC :cry:
lisa-cs: we already had a support ticket from a paying customer at 09:20 complaining about timeouts, forwarding their request ids now: req_8d9f3, req_b7c1a
marco.sre: deployed temporary circuit breaker rule to fail fast for long-running requests on this pool. will also scale burst pool by +2 nodes. applying now (deploy-bot below)
deploy-bot: Started rollout: cb-rule-short-circuit -> target: hosted-apne1-pool-3. Patch id 0x9f3a
anya.eng-runtime: can we capture a full runtime thread dump from one affected pod? attaching command:
```
kubectl exec -it pod/inference-runtime-77f5 -- curl -sS localhost:6060/debug/pprof/heap
```
devon.ops: creating a priority trace to capture slow path. running `trace-collector --since 2026-03-18T09:10Z --labels=apne-hosted`
marco.sre: quick mitigation notes: 1) short-circuit cb enabled 2) burst +2 nodes 3) disabled a queued_batching flag temporarily on this pool
anya.eng-runtime: after cb rollout we still see some 502s from older connections. suspect keepalive/reset issues between apigw and runtime sidecar
jamie-product: customers impacted? list of org ids please so CS can prioritize comms
lisa-cs: impacted orgs: org-443, org-998 (high volume), org-1023 (enterprise). I've queued an SMS update to org-998 lead.
marco.sre: action item list (short):
- anya -> collect heap/profile for 2 affected pods + upload to s3 (due EOD)
- devon -> confirm autoscaler bumped pool and left headroom (10m)
- lisa-cs -> send templated comms + 1:1 for org-998 (ASAP)
- jamie-product -> coordinate SLA note + rollback plan (due 24h)
anya.eng-runtime: collected profiles, uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/3372109876/profiles.tar.gz. seeing KV cache stall around 300-600ms followed by OOM-ish GC spikes in one pod
marco.sre: start a focused postmortem doc when stable. template: incident summary, timeline, root cause hypotheses, remediation, follow-ups. I'll create a stub in /docs/incidents/3372109876-postmortem.md
devon.ops: autoscaler confirmed bump, nodes added at 09:16, scaled down at 09:52. CPU avg on pool peaked at 82%
anya.eng-runtime: reproduced locally with synthetic workload that resembles org-998 request pattern (long prefix + streaming). KV cache eviction + concurrent warmup caused retry storm on runtime leading to queues building up
marco.sre: hypothesized RCA: cache warmup + concurrent long-prefix streaming -> blocking path in runtime that doesn't yield to new requests -> queue explosion -> timeouts -> upstream 502/504s. Secondary factor: keepalive reset churn exposing older connection semantics
jamie-product: proposed fixes: 1) change cache warmup to background async with rate limit 2) hard limit per-connection token budget 3) increase keepalive timeout compatibility. prioritize (1) asap
lisa-cs: customers notified with interim mitigation note. awaiting internal postmortem to share root cause and ETA for fixes
marco.sre: tagging owners and due dates: anya (RCA doc + profile analysis) due today EOD; devon (autoscaler & cb tuning) due tomorrow 09:00Z; jamie (SLA comm + prod plan) due 24h; infra followup for keepalive semantics (owner: eng-infra, pinged)
sre_bot: Reminder set: postmortem doc draft due in 24 hours for thread 3372109876
anya.eng-runtime: next steps, will implement a small patch to make cache fill async and add a non-blocking path for streaming requests. will open PR and request review from marco and devon
marco.sre: good. let's avoid a full rollback; target a canary release to 5% traffic once PR lands and monitor 5xx and queue depth for 30m
devon.ops: logged runbook entry: if 5xx > 1% for 10m, enable cb short-circuit + add burst nodes. saving to ops-runbook/incidents/cache-warmup.json
lisa-cs: thanks team. I'll follow up with affected customers after postmortem posted. sending summary to account teams now :thumbsup:
marco.sre: closing war room for now — monitoring in follow-up channel. file attachments (profiles + traces) linked in the postmortem stub. will reopen if errors reappear.
